newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Arrest sought for S.Korean journalist over report.
newsitem.headline: Arrest sought for S.Korean journalist over report.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said on Monday they were seeking an arrest warrant for a local journalist who wrote in a report that President Kim Young-sam's office secretly provided flour to North Korea.
Lee Kyo-kwan, 33, a reporter for weekly magazine Sisa Journal, was being questioned by investigators after Kim's chief secretary sued him for defamation, they said.

Lee said in a recent report that the presidential Blue House secretly provided 5,000 tonnes of flour to North Korea earlier this year in a bid to seek help from Pyongyang for co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup soccer games.
The chief presidential secretary, Kim Kwang-il, filed a suit last week, saying Lee's article was groundless and that it defamed the presidential office.
Red Cross officials have said North Korea faces a long-term problem in feeding itself after floods and heavy rains this year and last year destroyed part of its arable land.
FIFA, world soccer's governing body, has awarded Japan and South Korea to co-host the 2002 World Cup.
"We are seeking an arrest warrant for Lee after we could not find evidence that the story was correct," a state prosecutor told Reuters.
Defamation through publication is a criminal offence punishable by up to seven years in jail in South Korea.
